title: ’I have no problem meeting them’: Trump offers face-to-face meeting with Iran leaders
byline: US President Donald Trump said he was willing to meet with Iranian leaders if it meant a breakthrough could be reached in the Iran war peace talks.

title: Sri Lanka to retain QR fuel system indefinitely amid global oil uncertainty
byline: Against the backdrop of fluctuating global fuel prices, Sri Lanka has decided to continue with the QR code system for the rationalisation of fuel distribution indefinitely, an official said.

title: Tim Cook to step down as Apple CEO
byline: Apple CEO Tim Cook is stepping down from the job he inherited from the late Steve Jobs, ending a nearly 15-year reign that saw the company’s market value soar by more than $3.6 trillion during an iPhone-fuelled era of prosperity.

title: Namal accuses Govt of politicising easter attacks probe
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa has accused the government of politicising investigations into the Easter Sunday attacks, alleging selective action and misplaced blame.

title: All the airlines cancelling flights and adding extra charges amid jet fuel crisis
byline: The global aviation industry is facing significant turbulence following a dramatic surge in jet fuel prices, driven by the escalating US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

title: Vietnamese monks arrive for ‘Ehipassiko’ peace walk, accompanied by dog ‘Aloka’
byline: A group of Vietnamese monks based in the United States, including Venerables Pannakara and Ratanaguna, arrived in Sri Lanka early this morning (21) to take part in the global peace initiative “Ehipassiko”, A Global Walk for Peace.

title: Heavy rains above 100mm expected across several provinces today
byline: The Meteorology Department says showers or thundershowers will occur in most parts of the island after 1.00 p.m. today (21).

title: Former MP Premalal Jayasekara arrested in Nuwara Eliya
byline: Former Member of Parliament Premalal Jayasekara, known as ’’Choka Malli,’’ has been arrested by the Nuwara Eliya Police.

title: Youth arrested over fake bank website scam
byline: A 22-year-old suspect from Minuwangoda has been arrested over an alleged financial fraud involving a counterfeit website imitating a private bank, Sri Lanka Police said.

title: Chaotic weather grips Sri Lanka with rain and heat warnings
byline: Sri Lanka is expected to experience a mix of wet and warm conditions, creating a hybrid climate across the island, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Get the assistance of a foreign Central Bank to probe NDB issue: Ravi K
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake should intervene and get the assistance of any foreign Central Bank to carry out a forensic audit to conduct a probe on Rs 13.2 billion fraud at the National Development Bank (NDB), Democratic National Alliance (DNA) MP Ravi Karunanayake said yesterday.

title: AWC urges Vietnamese monk to fast-track delayed animal welfare act
byline: The Animal Welfare Coalition (AWC) has issued an appeal to Vietnamese monk Venerable Pannakara Thera urging immediate intervention to expedite the long-delayed Animal Welfare Act, describing it as a critical step toward protecting Sri Lanka’s street animals.

title: Apostolic Nuncio stresses forgiveness for Easter Sunday attackers
byline: Apostolic Nuncio (Vatican Ambassador to Sri Lanka) Monsignor Andrez Jozwowlez today stressed the need for forgiveness for the Easter Sunday attackers, while noting that forgiveness can come only after the truth behind the attacks is established.

title: Rs. 1.2 bn allocated to compensate farmers affected by Nilwala salt barrier
byline: The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board says that Rs. 1,200 million has been allocated under the 2026 Budget to compensate farmers for crop damage caused by the saltwater barrier constructed along the Nilwala River.

title: Trump’s Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer latest to leave administration
byline: US Secretary of Labour Lori Chavez-DeRemer will be leaving her post in the administration of President Donald Trump, the White House has said.

title: President backs ‘Walk for Peace’ initiative across Sri Lanka
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has expressed his full support for the “Walk for Peace” journey, which officially commenced in Sri Lanka today (April 21).

title: Controversy erupts over alleged “no dog removal” directive linked to “Aloka” initiative
byline: A heated controversy has emerged after the Animal Welfare Coalition (AWC) claimed that a special notice had been issued to police and local government authorities saying that “no street dogs need to be removed through Aloka,” sparking confusion and debate over the authenticity and intent of the directive.

title: Iran files complaint at UN over the US’s ‘illegal, barbarous’ ship seizure
byline: Iran’s Foreign Ministry has lodged a formal complaint with the UN secretary-general and the International Maritime Organization over the US seizure of the Iranian merchant vessel Touska on Monday, condemning it as an “illegal and barbarous act” that violates both international law and the ceasefire agreement.

title: Probe launched after poisoning of 10 dogs in Kalawewa
byline: A disturbing incident involving the poisoning of 10 dogs in the Kalawewa area yesterday has triggered widespread public outrage and prompted swift intervention by animal welfare activists.

title: Protect the planet, CEJ urges public on earth day
byline: On the occasion of International Earth Day, the Centre for Environmental Justice (CEJ) has called on the public to reaffirm their commitment to environmental justice, biodiversity protection and climate resilience, stressing that safeguarding the planet is the responsibility of every citizen.

title: UN Resident Coordinator calls for completion of Easter Sunday attack probes
byline: UN Resident Coordinator Mac-Andre Franche today called for a quick completion of probes carried out into the Easter Sunday bomb attacks.

title: Heat index alert issued as “caution level” temperatures expected across island
byline: A widespread heat alert has been issued for almost all provinces, warning that the “feels-like” temperature could rise to caution level during daytime hours across large parts of Sri Lanka.

title: Dhamma school teacher exam 2026 application deadline extended
byline: The Buddhist Affairs Department has extended the application deadline for the 2026 Dhamma School Teacher Certificate Examination.

title: Low-floor bus service launched in Makumbura with priority for disabled passengers
byline: A pilot low-floor bus service aimed at providing safe, comfortable and reliable transport for persons with disabilities and special needs was launched today ( 21) at the Makumbura Multimodal Transport Center under the government’s “Clean Sri Lanka” programme.

title: Scammers impersonating as Iran demanding crypto fees for safe Hormuz passage
byline: Greek maritime risk management firm MARISKS has warned that unknown actors, purporting to be Iranian authorities, have delivered messages to some shipping companies demanding transit fees in cryptocurrencies in return for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Migrants in Spain queue to apply for mass legalisation programme
byline: Migrants in Spain have queued up to apply for the country’s mass legalisation programme on Monday.

title: War in Iran is causing biggest energy crisis in history, IEA says
byline: The conflict between Iran and the United States and Israel is creating the ​worst energy crisis ever faced by the ‌world, the head of the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.

title: Iran’s World Cup participation depends on team’s safety in the US: Minister
byline: Iran’s football team is preparing for the World Cup, but a final decision on its participation in the tournament will be taken by the government, the country’s sport minister says.

title: Police deny claims STF receiving motorcycles from Avant Garde
byline: Sri Lanka Police have denied claims circulating on social media that the Special Task Force (STF) is set to receive motorcycles from Avant Garde.

title: US-intercepted tanker moves near Sri Lanka waters
byline: Ship-tracking data indicates that a crude oil tanker intercepted by the US military in the Indian Ocean made a sharp change of course in the early hours of this morning and is now broadcasting its position around 700km (430 miles) south-east of Sri Lanka.

title: We would arrest Netanyahu, says Hungary’s incoming PM
byline: Hungary’s incoming prime minister has said he’ll stop the country’s withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC).

title: Government declares Vesak Week from May 27 to June 2
byline: The official programme for the 2026 Vesak Festival has been announced by the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government.

title: Central expressway sections to open in 2027 and 2028: RDA
byline: The Road Development Authority (RDA) has announced that key sections of the Central Expressway are scheduled to be opened in phases over the coming years.

title: MLFF system to replace cash toll payments on expressways
byline: Amid ongoing moves to reduce cash handling on expressways, the Road Development Authority (RDA) is preparing to introduce a new toll collection system known as Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF), RDA Director General Anuradha Hettiarachchi said.

title: US, Iran exchange threats as fragile ceasefire set to expire
byline: Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said Iran is “prepared to reveal new cards on the battlefield” after United States President Donald Trump threatened Tehran with “problems like they’ve never seen before” if the two-week ceasefire expires on Wednesday without a deal.

title: INS NIREEKSHAK makes port call in Colombo
byline: The Indian Navy Ship (INS) NIREEKSHAK arrived in Sri Lanka for Operational Turnaround (OTR) and a training visit today. The Sri Lanka Navy welcomed the visiting ship at the port of Colombo in accordance with time-honoured naval traditions.

title: Anura Karunathilaka assumes duties as Energy Minister
byline: Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Anura Karunathilaka today assumed duties as the Minister of Energy at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Energy premises.

title: Police refute claims of planned bomb attacks in Colombo
byline: Sri Lanka Police have dismissed as “completely false” reports circulating on social media and some websites claiming that a suspect was planning a series of bomb attacks in Colombo and other crowded areas.

title: Joint Opposition questions legality behind decision for trial-at-bar to hear RW case
byline: The Joint Opposition today questioned the legality behind the decision to set up a trial-at-bar to take up the case against former President Ranil Wickremesinghe.

title: Trump urges Iran to free 8 women allegedly facing execution
byline: US President Donald Trump has appealed to Tehran to release eight women reportedly facing execution, framing the move as a vital gesture of goodwill before the high-stakes second round of negotiations in Pakistan.

title: Sri Lanka receives $100,000 from Philippines for cyclone recovery
byline: Sri Lanka has received a donation of $100,000 from the Philippines to support reconstruction and recovery efforts following the impact of Cyclone Ditwah.

title: Govt. can’t control prices, but supply will remain uninterrupted: New Energy Minister
byline: New Energy Minister Anura Karunathilake said that the government’s primary objective remains the consistent and uninterrupted delivery of essential services, specifically electricity and fuel, to the public.

title: Pakistan urges US, Iran to extend truce
byline: Pakistan on Tuesday urged the United States and Iran to extend their two-week ceasefire, emphasizing the need for dialogue and diplomacy.

title: Ofcom investigating Telegram over child sexual abuse material concerns
byline: The UK media regulator has launched an investigation into Telegram over concerns it may be failing to prevent child sexual abuse material (CSAM) being shared.

title: 50 foreign nationals arrested in Negombo for visa overstay
byline: A total of 50 foreign nationals have been arrested by officers of the Investigation Division of the Immigration and Emigration Department for overstaying their visas, authorities said.

title: Heavy rains flood roads in Nawalapitiya, disrupt traffic
byline: A brief but intense spell of rain in Nawalapitiya on the afternoon of April 21 left key roads inundated, with flooding reported at the town bus stand and along the Nawalapitiya–Kandy Road, severely disrupting traffic.

title: Iran’s World Cup participation depends on team’s safety in the US: Minister
byline: Iran’s football team is preparing for the World Cup, but a final decision on its participation in the tournament will be taken by the government, the country’s sport minister says.

title: We would arrest Netanyahu, says Hungary’s incoming PM
byline: Hungary’s incoming prime minister has said he’ll stop the country’s withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC).

byline: Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said Iran is “prepared to reveal new cards on the battlefield” after United States President Donald Trump threatened Tehran with “problems like they’ve never seen before” if the two-week ceasefire expires on Wednesday without a deal.
